title: System Lockout — Ignition Failure
shortDescription: The furnace has locked out after multiple failed ignition attempts.
fullDescription: One red flash on a Trane or American Standard furnace indicates a system lockout due to failed ignition. The control board tried to light the burners the maximum number of times without success. The system will auto-reset after a waiting period or can be manually reset by cycling power.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave immediately and call your gas company. Do not continue to reset the furnace if it repeatedly fails to ignite.

causes.cause: Weak or failed hot surface igniter
Gas valve issue or low gas pressure

symptoms: One red LED flash on control board
No heat produced
Clicking or humming during ignition attempts
Furnace cycles through startup but never lights

fixSteps.title: Reset the System
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace power switch, wait 30 seconds, turn it back on. Watch the ignition sequence.

fixSteps.title: Clean Flame Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean the flame sensor rod with fine emery cloth. Reinstall and test.

fixSteps.title: Check Igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Observe if the igniter glows during the ignition sequence. Test resistance with a multimeter (10-200 ohms is typical).

fixSteps.title: Verify Gas Supply
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the gas shutoff valve near the furnace is fully open. Verify other gas appliances work.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning the flame sensor and checking the igniter does not resolve the lockout, or if you suspect a gas supply problem.

faq.q: Are Trane and American Standard the same?
faq.a: Trane and American Standard furnaces are made by the same manufacturer and share the same diagnostic codes and many of the same parts.

faq.q: How long does the lockout last?
faq.a: Typically 1-3 hours for auto-reset. You can manually reset by cycling the power switch.

faq.q: What is the most common cause?
faq.a: A dirty flame sensor is the most common cause of ignition lockout on Trane furnaces. Cleaning it takes only a few minutes.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: The pressure switch did not close, indicating a draft or venting problem.
fullDescription: Two red flashes on a Trane furnace indicate the pressure switch failed to close after the draft inducer motor started. This safety device verifies proper exhaust venting before allowing gas to flow.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Never bypass the pressure switch. If you smell gas, evacuate and call your gas company.

causes.cause: Blocked exhaust or intake vent pipe
Cracked or kinked pressure switch hose
Weak or failing draft inducer motor

symptoms: Two red LED flashes
Draft inducer runs but burners never light
Furnace shuts down after inducer startup
Humming from inducer without progression to ignition

fixSteps.title: Check Vent Pipes
fixSteps.instruction: Go outside and inspect exhaust and intake vent pipes for blockages from ice, snow, nests, or debris.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pressure Hose
fixSteps.instruction: Check the small rubber hose from the pressure switch to the inducer. Ensure it is connected at both ends with no cracks or water inside.

fixSteps.title: Clear Condensate Drain
fixSteps.instruction: For 90%+ efficiency models, check the condensate drain and trap for clogs. Flush with warm water.

fixSteps.title: Test Pressure Switch
fixSteps.instruction: With inducer running, test for continuity across the pressure switch. It should show closed (continuity) when the inducer is operating.

whenToCallPro: If vents are clear, hose is good, and the error persists. The inducer motor or pressure switch may need replacement.

faq.q: Why does this code come up in winter?
faq.a: Ice and snow can block the outdoor exhaust/intake vents, especially during severe cold. Check them after storms.

faq.q: Can I jump the pressure switch?
faq.a: Never. The pressure switch ensures combustion gases are properly vented. Bypassing it risks CO poisoning.

faq.q: What does the pressure switch do?
faq.a: It verifies the draft inducer is creating enough airflow to safely exhaust combustion gases before allowing gas to flow to the burners.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: Pressure switch is closed before the draft inducer starts.
fullDescription: Three red flashes indicate the pressure switch is reading closed before the draft inducer motor has started. This could be a mechanically stuck switch, wiring fault, or water in the pressure hose.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: A stuck-closed pressure switch defeats a critical safety check. Do not operate the furnace until this is resolved.

causes.cause: Water trapped in pressure switch hose
Wiring short across pressure switch terminals

symptoms: Three red LED flashes
Furnace will not start at all
Error appears immediately on heat call
Draft inducer may not start

fixSteps.title: Drain Pressure Hose
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the pressure switch hose and check for trapped water. Drain and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Test Switch State
fixSteps.instruction: With power off and inducer not running, check continuity across the pressure switch. It should be open (no continuity).

fixSteps.title: Check Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect wires to the pressure switch for damage or shorts that could make the switch appear closed.

fixSteps.title: Replace Pressure Switch
fixSteps.instruction: If the switch tests as stuck closed, replace it with the correct part for your Trane model.

whenToCallPro: If you cannot determine why the switch is stuck or if replacement does not resolve the issue.

faq.q: Can condensation cause this?
faq.a: Yes, water from condensation can get trapped in the pressure switch hose and create a false closed reading.

faq.q: Is this dangerous?
faq.a: A stuck-closed pressure switch could theoretically allow the furnace to fire without proper venting. The control board detects this and prevents operation.

faq.q: How do I know which pressure switch to buy?
faq.a: Match the part number on the existing switch or use your Trane model number to find the correct replacement.

title: Open High Limit Switch — Overheating
shortDescription: The furnace has overheated and the high limit safety switch has tripped.
fullDescription: Four red flashes on a Trane furnace indicate the high temperature limit switch has opened due to overheating. This is typically caused by restricted airflow through the furnace.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Repeated overheating can crack the heat exchanger, which can lead to carbon monoxide leakage. Ensure CO detectors are functional. Do not ignore repeated limit switch trips.

causes.cause: Dirty evaporator coil (AC coil above furnace)

symptoms: Four red LED flashes
Furnace starts but shuts off after a few minutes
Very hot air before shutdown
Burning smell
Repeated short cycling

fixSteps.title: Replace Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Check and replace the air filter immediately. This is the most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Open All Vents
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure all supply and return vents throughout the home are open and unobstructed.

fixSteps.title: Check Blower Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Set thermostat fan to ON. The blower should run. If not, the motor or capacitor may be faulty.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Evaporator Coil
fixSteps.instruction: If visible, check the evaporator coil above the furnace for heavy dust buildup that restricts airflow.

whenToCallPro: If the filter is clean, vents are open, and the furnace still overheats. The blower motor or heat exchanger needs inspection.

faq.q: Why does my Trane furnace keep overheating?
faq.a: The most common cause is a dirty air filter. Less common causes include a failing blower motor, dirty evaporator coil, or blocked ductwork.

faq.q: Can closing vents save energy?
faq.a: No, closing vents increases pressure and reduces airflow through the furnace, which can cause overheating. Keep all vents open.

faq.q: How serious is repeated overheating?
faq.a: Very serious. It can crack the heat exchanger over time, leading to expensive repairs and potential CO exposure.

title: Flame Sensed Without Gas Valve Command
shortDescription: Flame detected when the gas valve should be off — possible gas valve leak.
fullDescription: Five red flashes on a Trane furnace indicate flame is being detected when the gas valve has not been commanded to open. This is a critical safety condition.
safetyWarning: CRITICAL: This may indicate a leaking gas valve. If you smell gas, leave immediately and call 911 or your gas company. Do not operate any switches.

causes.cause: Flame sensor wiring shorted to ground

symptoms: Five red LED flashes
Furnace locked out immediately
Possible gas odor
Error before ignition sequence starts

fixSteps.title: Check for Gas Odor
fixSteps.instruction: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company or 911.

fixSteps.title: Shut Down System
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace power switch and close the gas shutoff valve.

fixSteps.title: Check Flame Sensor Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, inspect the flame sensor wire for damage or grounding against the chassis.

fixSteps.title: Call a Professional
fixSteps.instruction: This code requires professional diagnosis of the gas valve and flame sensing circuit.

whenToCallPro: Immediately. This is a safety-critical code.

faq.q: Is this an emergency?
faq.a: If you smell gas, yes. Even without a gas smell, have it inspected promptly as the gas valve may have an intermittent leak.

faq.q: Can I fix this myself?
faq.a: No. Gas valve issues must be diagnosed and repaired by a licensed HVAC technician.

faq.q: How much does a Trane gas valve cost?
faq.a: Parts cost $100-$300, with total repair typically $250-$700.

title: Power or Wiring Fault — Reversed Polarity
shortDescription: Line voltage polarity is reversed or ground is missing.
fullDescription: Six red flashes indicate the Trane furnace control board has detected reversed hot/neutral polarity or a grounding problem in the power supply wiring.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Turn off power at the breaker before checking any electrical connections.

causes.cause: Hot and neutral wires swapped at furnace
Polarity issue at circuit breaker panel

symptoms: Six red LED flashes
Furnace will not operate
May follow recent electrical work
Flame sensor may not detect flame

fixSteps.title: Kill Power
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace breaker before any inspection.

fixSteps.title: Check Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Use a voltage tester to verify hot and neutral are on the correct terminals at the furnace power connection.

fixSteps.title: Verify Ground
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the ground wire is securely attached to the furnace chassis.

fixSteps.title: Test Supply Circuit
fixSteps.instruction: Test the outlet or disconnect switch feeding the furnace for correct polarity and grounding.

whenToCallPro: If you are not comfortable with electrical wiring or if correcting polarity does not resolve the issue.

faq.q: Why does polarity matter?
faq.a: The flame sensing circuit needs proper polarity to work. Reversed polarity causes the flame sensor to fail.

faq.q: Is this a common problem?
faq.a: It is fairly common after new furnace installation or electrical work when wires get swapped.

faq.q: Can an outlet tester check this?
faq.a: Yes, an inexpensive outlet tester from the hardware store can verify polarity and grounding if the furnace is plug-connected.

title: Gas Valve Circuit Error
shortDescription: The control board has detected an abnormal condition in the gas valve wiring.
fullDescription: Seven red flashes on a Trane furnace indicate a fault in the gas valve circuit — either an open or shorted gas valve coil, or a wiring problem between the control board and the gas valve.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Do not attempt to bypass or manually operate the gas valve. If you smell gas, leave immediately and call your gas company.

causes.cause: Loose or damaged wiring to gas valve
Control board gas valve relay failure

symptoms: Seven red LED flashes
Igniter may glow but no gas flows
No clicking from gas valve
Furnace locked out during ignition sequence

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off power for 60 seconds and restore to check for transient fault.

fixSteps.title: Check Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, inspect the wire harness between the control board and gas valve for loose or damaged connections.

fixSteps.title: Test Gas Valve Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across the gas valve coil terminals. Compare to manufacturer specs.

fixSteps.title: Call Professional
fixSteps.instruction: Gas valve replacement requires a licensed technician who can properly test for leaks after installation.

whenToCallPro: For any gas valve replacement. This is not a DIY repair.

faq.q: Can I check the gas valve myself?
faq.a: You can check the wiring and coil resistance, but actual valve replacement must be done by a professional.

faq.q: How much is a Trane gas valve?
faq.a: The part costs $100-$300, with total installed cost of $250-$700.

faq.q: Could this just be a wiring issue?
faq.a: Yes, sometimes a loose connector is the only problem. Checking wiring is a reasonable first step.

title: Igniter Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The hot surface igniter circuit is open or has abnormal resistance.
fullDescription: Eight red flashes on a Trane furnace indicate the control board has detected a problem with the igniter circuit. The igniter is likely broken (open circuit) and cannot heat up to ignite the gas.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Turn off the furnace before working on the igniter. Do not touch the igniter element with bare hands.
symptoms: Eight red LED flashes
Igniter does not glow
Draft inducer runs but ignition never begins
No heat produced

fixSteps.title: Inspect Igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Visually check for cracks in the igniter element. Even hairline cracks cause failure.

fixSteps.title: Check Connections
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure the wire connector at the igniter is firmly seated.

fixSteps.title: Test Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect and measure igniter resistance. Good: 10-200 ohms. OL (open): broken.

fixSteps.title: Replace Igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the mounting screw, swap the igniter. Handle the new one by the base only.

whenToCallPro: If replacing the igniter does not fix the issue, or if you are not comfortable accessing the burner compartment.

faq.q: How often do igniters fail?
faq.a: Typical lifespan is 3-7 years. Silicon nitride igniters last longer than silicon carbide.

faq.q: Can I use a universal igniter?
faq.a: Universal igniters may work but OEM Trane replacements ensure proper fit and performance.

faq.q: Why should I not touch the igniter?
faq.a: Skin oils create hot spots that cause premature cracking. Always handle by the ceramic base or use gloves.

title: Low Flame Signal / Weak Flame
shortDescription: The flame sensor is detecting a weak flame signal, causing intermittent shutdowns.
fullDescription: Nine red flashes on a Trane furnace indicate the flame sensor microamp reading is below the minimum threshold. The flame may be present but the sensor cannot adequately detect it, usually due to a dirty sensor or improper gas combustion.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Weak or improper combustion can produce carbon monoxide. Ensure CO detectors are working. If flames appear yellow or abnormal, turn off the furnace.
symptoms: Nine red LED flashes
Furnace lights but shuts off after a few seconds
Intermittent operation
Weak or yellow flame

fixSteps.title: Clean Flame Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and clean the flame sensor rod with fine emery cloth. This resolves the issue most of the time.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor Insulator
fixSteps.instruction: Check the ceramic insulator for cracks. Replace the sensor if the insulator is damaged.

fixSteps.title: Observe Flame
fixSteps.instruction: Watch the burner flames. Blue with small yellow tips is normal. All yellow or lazy flames indicate combustion problems.

fixSteps.title: Check Gas Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: A technician can measure manifold gas pressure to ensure proper combustion.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning the flame sensor does not resolve the issue or if the flame color is abnormal.

faq.q: How do I find the flame sensor?
faq.a: The flame sensor is a thin metal rod mounted on a porcelain insulator, located in the burner assembly area. It has one wire attached.

faq.q: What is a good flame sensor reading?
faq.a: A healthy reading is typically 1.5-6 microamps. Below 1 microamp causes intermittent shutdowns.

faq.q: How often should I clean it?
faq.a: Annually during maintenance, or whenever the furnace starts shutting down shortly after ignition.

title: Rollout Limit Switch Open
shortDescription: The flame rollout safety switch has tripped, indicating flames escaping the combustion chamber.
fullDescription: Ten red flashes indicate the rollout limit switch has opened due to flames extending beyond the normal combustion area. This is a serious safety condition often caused by a blocked heat exchanger.
safetyWarning: CRITICAL: Flame rollout is extremely dangerous. It risks fire and carbon monoxide exposure. Turn off the furnace immediately and call a professional. Do not reset the rollout switch.
symptoms: Ten red LED flashes
Scorch marks on furnace cabinet
Strong burning smell
Visible flames outside burner area
CO detector may alarm

fixSteps.title: Shut Down Immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace power and gas supply valve right away.

fixSteps.title: Check CO Detectors
fixSteps.instruction: If CO detectors alarm, evacuate and call 911.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Exhaust Vent
fixSteps.instruction: Look for blockages in the exhaust vent but do not restart the furnace.

fixSteps.title: Call Professional
fixSteps.instruction: A licensed technician must inspect the heat exchanger before the furnace can be operated safely.

whenToCallPro: Immediately. Do not operate the furnace until professionally inspected.

faq.q: What causes flame rollout?
faq.a: Usually a blocked heat exchanger, blocked exhaust, or excessive gas pressure forcing flames out of the combustion chamber.

faq.q: Can I reset the rollout switch?
faq.a: Never reset it without professional inspection. The cause must be found and fixed first.

faq.q: Is a heat exchanger replacement worth it?
faq.a: Heat exchangers cost $1,000-$3,000+. For furnaces over 15 years old, full replacement is often more economical.

title: External Lockout / Power Reset Required
shortDescription: A continuous red LED indicates the system is in external lockout and requires a manual power reset.
fullDescription: A steady red LED (not blinking) on some Trane furnaces indicates an external lockout condition that requires cycling the furnace power to reset. The system will not auto-reset from this state.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas at any time, leave and call your gas company. If the lockout recurs after reset, do not keep resetting — call for service.

causes.cause: Repeated safety lockouts triggering hard lockout

symptoms: Steady red LED
Furnace completely non-responsive
Will not start even when thermostat calls
Requires manual power cycle

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace power switch or breaker. Wait 30-60 seconds. Restore power. The LED pattern after reset will indicate the underlying fault.

fixSteps.title: Watch for Error Code
fixSteps.instruction: After reset, watch the LED closely. If it shows a blink pattern before going to steady red again, note the number of blinks — that is the underlying fault code.

fixSteps.title: Address Root Cause
fixSteps.instruction: Use the blink code observed after reset to determine and fix the underlying issue before it causes another lockout.

fixSteps.title: Call Professional
fixSteps.instruction: If the furnace goes to steady red repeatedly, a professional needs to diagnose the recurring fault.

whenToCallPro: If the furnace repeatedly returns to a steady red lockout after being reset.

faq.q: How do I reset my Trane furnace?
faq.a: Turn off the power switch near the furnace (or the breaker), wait 30-60 seconds, then turn it back on.

faq.q: Why does it keep going to solid red?
faq.a: An underlying fault (like a bad igniter or pressure switch issue) is causing repeated lockouts. The root cause must be fixed.

faq.q: Is this an emergency?
faq.a: Not typically, unless you smell gas. It means the furnace has shut down safely but needs attention.

title: Normal Operation — Call for Heat Active
shortDescription: A steady green LED indicates the furnace is operating normally during a heating cycle.
fullDescription: On Trane furnaces with dual or multi-color LEDs, a steady green light indicates the system is in a normal heating cycle. The thermostat is calling for heat and the furnace is running properly.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Even during normal operation, maintain CO detectors and keep the furnace area clear.

causes.cause: If house is cold despite green light, check airflow

symptoms: Steady green LED
Warm air from vents
Normal operating sounds
Thermostat shows heating active

fixSteps.title: Confirm Heat Output
fixSteps.instruction: Check that warm air is coming from supply vents.

fixSteps.title: Check Filter
fixSteps.instruction: If airflow seems weak, check the air filter.

fixSteps.title: Verify Vent Positions
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure all supply and return vents are open.

fixSteps.title: Monitor Cycle Length
fixSteps.instruction: Normal cycles are 10-20 minutes. Very short cycles suggest a problem.

whenToCallPro: Only if the furnace runs but the home does not warm adequately.

faq.q: Is steady green an error?
faq.a: No, it means the furnace is running a normal heating cycle.

faq.q: How long should the green light stay on?
faq.a: The green light stays on during the heating cycle, typically 10-20 minutes per cycle.

faq.q: What if the green light is on but no heat?
faq.a: Check that the blower fan is running. If the inducer and burners are on but the blower is not, the blower motor or capacitor may be faulty.

title: No Power to Control Board
shortDescription: No LED visible indicates the control board has no power.
fullDescription: When no LED is illuminated on the Trane furnace control board, the board is not receiving power. Check the breaker, power switch, board fuse, and transformer.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: Turn off the gas supply before troubleshooting electrical issues.
symptoms: No LED on control board
Furnace completely dead
Thermostat may be blank
No sounds at all

fixSteps.title: Check Breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Find and reset the furnace breaker if tripped.

fixSteps.title: Check Power Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the furnace power switch is in the ON position.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Board Fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Check the fuse on the control board. Replace if blown (match the amperage).

fixSteps.title: Test Transformer
fixSteps.instruction: Check for 24VAC output from the transformer. If no output with 120V input, the transformer has failed.

whenToCallPro: If the breaker trips repeatedly or the transformer has failed.

faq.q: Why does the breaker keep tripping?
faq.a: This usually indicates a short circuit in the furnace wiring, a failing blower motor, or a bad breaker. Have it inspected.

faq.q: What fuse does my Trane furnace use?
faq.a: Most use a 3A or 5A automotive-style fuse. Check the existing fuse or manual for the correct rating.

faq.q: Why does the fuse keep blowing?
faq.a: Repeated blown fuses usually indicate a short in the thermostat wiring or at the thermostat itself.

title: Rollout Limit Manual Reset Required
shortDescription: The flame rollout switch with manual reset has tripped.
fullDescription: Eleven red flashes on some Trane models indicate the manual-reset rollout limit switch has tripped. A technician must determine the cause and manually reset the switch.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave immediately and call your gas company.
symptoms: 11-red-flash LED pattern
System malfunction
No heat or intermittent heat
Unusual sounds or behavior

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off furnace power for 30 seconds, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Check Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the air filter if dirty.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for loose connections.

fixSteps.title: Call Professional
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, professional diagnosis is needed.

whenToCallPro: If basic troubleshooting does not resolve the error.

faq.q: What does 11-red-flash mean?
faq.a: The flame rollout switch with manual reset has tripped.

faq.q: Is this serious?
faq.a: It depends on the specific code. Some are minor and some need immediate attention.

faq.q: How much will repair cost?
faq.a: $100-$500 depending on the issue.

title: Blower Motor Speed Error
shortDescription: The blower motor is not running at the expected speed.
fullDescription: Twelve red flashes indicate the blower motor is not reaching the commanded speed. This could be due to a failing motor, bad capacitor, or ECM motor control issue.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave immediately and call your gas company.
symptoms: 12-red-flash LED pattern
System malfunction
No heat or intermittent heat
Unusual sounds or behavior

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off furnace power for 30 seconds, then restore.

fixSteps.title: Check Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the air filter if dirty.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check for loose connections.

fixSteps.title: Call Professional
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, professional diagnosis is needed.

whenToCallPro: If basic troubleshooting does not resolve the error.

faq.q: What does 12-red-flash mean?
faq.a: The blower motor is not running at the expected speed.

faq.q: Is this serious?
faq.a: It depends on the specific code. Some are minor and some need immediate attention.

faq.q: How much will repair cost?
faq.a: $100-$500 depending on the issue.

title: Ignition Failure — Hot Surface Igniter Fault
shortDescription: The hot surface igniter is not heating to the temperature needed to light the burners.
fullDescription: This Trane furnace fault indicates the hot surface igniter (HSI) failed to reach proper glow temperature, or the control board sensed an open circuit on the igniter output. Without a glowing igniter the gas valve will not be authorized to open, so the burners never light and the cycle aborts after the trial-for-ignition period.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Cracked or burned-out hot surface igniter
Loose or corroded igniter wiring connection
Weak igniter — resistance drifting outside spec
Improper line voltage to the furnace

symptoms: Burners never light during a call for heat
Inducer runs but no glow visible at the igniter
Repeated retries followed by hard lockout
Cold air from registers when the blower runs

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle the Furnace
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the furnace disconnect off for 60 seconds, then back on, and watch the next ignition attempt through the inspection port.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the Igniter Visually
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the burner cover and look for a cracked, broken, or whitened igniter element. Any visible damage means replace it.

fixSteps.title: Measure Igniter Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, disconnect the igniter and measure resistance across its leads. A healthy silicon-nitride HSI typically reads 40–90 ohms; older silicon-carbide types read 50–200 ohms. Open or out-of-range = replace.

fixSteps.title: Check Igniter Connector and Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the molex/spade connector for corrosion, melted plastic, or loose pins. Reseat firmly and look for chafed wires along the routing.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Install the manufacturer-specified igniter, handling only by the ceramic base — skin oils shorten igniter life. Confirm the tip aligns with the carryover slot per the service manual.

whenToCallPro: If the new igniter also fails, if line voltage is unstable, or if the control board's igniter output reads incorrect voltage during trial-for-ignition.

faq.q: How long does a furnace igniter last?
faq.a: Most hot surface igniters last 4–7 years. Frequent short-cycling and handling the element with bare fingers shorten that life significantly.

faq.q: Can I clean an igniter instead of replacing it?
faq.a: No. The ceramic element cannot be cleaned safely. If it is contaminated or cracked, replacement is the only fix.

faq.q: Why did my new igniter fail quickly?
faq.a: The most common cause is touching the element with bare fingers during installation. Skin oils create hot spots that crack the ceramic.

title: Gas Valve Circuit Fault
shortDescription: The control board cannot drive the gas valve, or its feedback is out of range.
fullDescription: On this Trane furnace the integrated control sends 24 VAC to the main gas valve during trial-for-ignition, but the valve either does not open, draws unexpected current, or fails open-coil checks. The system locks out before any gas is released to the burners.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Open or shorted gas valve solenoid coil
Loose, broken, or corroded gas valve wiring

symptoms: No gas flow even with a glowing igniter
Audible relay click but no valve opening sound
Lockout posted on the first ignition attempt
Repeated retries with no flame ever established

fixSteps.title: Verify 24 VAC at Valve
fixSteps.instruction: With a multimeter on the gas valve terminals during trial-for-ignition, confirm 24 VAC ±10%. No voltage means a board or wiring issue, not a valve issue.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Valve Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check both leads for cracked insulation, loose spades, or green corrosion. Reseat or replace the harness as needed.

fixSteps.title: Test Valve Coil Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, measure across the coil terminals. Most 24 VAC valves read 30–80 ohms. Open or near-zero means the valve is bad.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Transformer Output
fixSteps.instruction: At the control transformer, verify 24–28 VAC under load. A weak transformer can drop voltage enough to keep the valve from pulling in.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Gas Valve
fixSteps.instruction: Replacement of the gas valve is a licensed-trade operation requiring a leak test on every joint with electronic detector and soap solution. Do not attempt without proper certification.

whenToCallPro: Replacement of any gas valve, regulator, or piping must be done by a licensed gas technician — a leak after reassembly is life-threatening.

faq.q: Can I clean a sticking gas valve?
faq.a: No. Modern valves are sealed and not field-serviceable. Replace, do not disassemble.

faq.q: How much does a furnace gas valve cost?
faq.a: Parts run $60–$220 depending on model. Professional replacement with leak test is typically $300–$700.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using the furnace?
faq.a: If the lockout repeats, leave the system off and the gas closed. Intermittent valve faults can become hazardous quickly.

title: Flame Sensed Out of Sequence
shortDescription: The control board detects flame at a time when the gas valve should be closed.
fullDescription: This Trane fault means the flame-sense rod is reporting flame current when no flame should be present — typically before the gas valve opens or after the trial-for-ignition has ended. The control treats this as a serious safety condition and locks the furnace out to prevent unburned gas accumulation.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Flame sensor shorted to ground or chassis
Moisture or carbon bridging on the flame-sense rod
Faulty integrated control module misreading sensor

symptoms: Furnace locks out immediately on call for heat
Burners may briefly fire then shut off with lockout
Diagnostic LED reports flame-sense fault repeatedly
No heat output despite thermostat calling

fixSteps.title: Cut Power and Inspect Burners
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off power and gas. Remove the burner cover and look for soot, water staining, or a flame sensor touching metal.

fixSteps.title: Clean the Flame-Sense Rod
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rod and gently polish with fine emery cloth. Wipe with a clean rag — do not use sandpaper coarser than 400 grit.

fixSteps.title: Verify Sensor Mounting
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the rod is not contacting the burner shell or any metal support. Reposition so it sits in the flame envelope without grounding.

fixSteps.title: Check for Gas Valve Leakby
fixSteps.instruction: With ignition disabled, watch the burners for any flame after the inducer purge. A momentary flame indicates a leaking gas valve, which must be replaced by a licensed pro.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Wiring to Board
fixSteps.instruction: Measure continuity from the sensor terminal back to the control board. Replace any harness that shows shorts to ground or open conductors.

whenToCallPro: Any time a leaking gas valve is suspected, the smell of gas is present, or the lockout returns immediately after cleaning the sensor.

faq.q: Is flame sensed when off a serious fault?
faq.a: Yes. It can mean unburned gas is entering the heat exchanger, which is a fire and CO hazard. Do not bypass the lockout.

faq.q: Can I keep using the furnace until a tech arrives?
faq.a: No. Leave the furnace off and the gas supply closed until the cause is identified.

faq.q: What is normal flame current?
faq.a: Most modern furnaces show 1.5–6 microamps of DC flame current with a clean rod and stable flame.

title: Integrated Control Module Internal Fault
shortDescription: The furnace control board reports an internal self-test failure.
fullDescription: This Trane fault means the integrated furnace control's onboard self-diagnostics detected a failure — RAM/EEPROM corruption, watchdog reset, or a relay that did not transition correctly. The control halts heat operation until the fault clears or the board is replaced.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Voltage spike or surge damaging the control
Moisture intrusion on the control board
Failed relay or capacitor on the board
Loose ground or polarity reversed at line voltage

symptoms: Diagnostic LED steady or rapid-flashing without a normal sequence
System cycles power and resets repeatedly
Multiple unrelated faults posted at once
Furnace ignores thermostat input entirely

fixSteps.title: Hard-Reset the Furnace
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off at the disconnect for 5 minutes, then restore. A clean power-up clears most transient faults.

fixSteps.title: Verify Line Voltage and Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm 120 VAC ±10% with hot/neutral/ground correctly oriented. Reversed polarity prevents flame sensing on most boards.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Board for Damage
fixSteps.instruction: Look for swollen capacitors, scorch marks, melted relays, or corroded traces — replace the board if any are present.

fixSteps.title: Tighten All Low-Voltage Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: A loose 24 VAC connection can cause spurious resets. Snug each spade and screw terminal.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Control Board
fixSteps.instruction: Install the manufacturer-specified board, transferring DIP switch / jumper settings exactly. Confirm normal sequencing on the next call for heat.

whenToCallPro: If the fault persists after a hard reset and verification of line voltage/polarity, the board likely needs replacement by a qualified technician.

faq.q: How much does a furnace control board cost?
faq.a: Parts run $150–$500. Total installed cost is typically $400–$900.

faq.q: Will a surge protector help?
faq.a: Yes. A whole-home or HVAC-rated surge protector can prevent spike damage to the control.

faq.q: Can I swap a board myself?
faq.a: Many homeowners can, but DIP switch settings and wire routing must match exactly. Mistakes cause unsafe operation.

title: Airflow Verification Failure
shortDescription: The blower did not reach commanded RPM, indicating an airflow or motor problem.
fullDescription: On this Trane furnace the variable-speed or ECM blower control reports that the motor failed to reach the RPM commanded by the integrated control. The system reduces firing rate or locks out to prevent heat-exchanger overheating.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Loose communication harness between board and motor
Incorrect blower speed configuration after install
Excessive external static pressure on duct system

symptoms: Reduced airflow at registers
Furnace cycles at lower-than-rated heat output
Blower hunts up and down in speed
Lockout posted with airflow or RPM-related code

fixSteps.title: Replace the Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Install a clean media filter rated for the airflow. Avoid restrictive 1" filters above MERV 11 unless duct sizing allows.

fixSteps.title: Measure Total External Static Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Use a manometer at the supply and return plenum. Compare to the design value (often 0.5" WC). Higher = duct restriction problem.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Motor Communication Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the harness between the integrated control and the ECM module. Look for damaged pins or chafed insulation.

fixSteps.title: Verify Blower Configuration
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm DIP switch / dial settings for the installed tonnage and heat speed match the rating-plate guidance.

fixSteps.title: Replace the ECM Module
fixSteps.instruction: If commanded speed is correct but actual speed is far off, replace the motor module per OEM procedure. ECM motors and modules are matched pairs on many models.

whenToCallPro: If external static pressure is high, the duct system may need professional rework. ECM motor/module replacement also requires a tech.

faq.q: Why is total external static pressure important?
faq.a: It tells you whether the duct system can deliver the airflow the furnace is rated for. Too high and the blower cannot move design CFM.

faq.q: Are ECM and PSC blowers interchangeable?
faq.a: Usually not. ECM systems require a matching control output and configuration.

faq.q: Will a higher-MERV filter cause this?
faq.a: Yes if the duct system is borderline. Use thicker media filters instead of restrictive 1" panels.

title: Thermostat / R-W Signal Issue
shortDescription: The control board sees an invalid or missing call from the thermostat.
fullDescription: This Trane fault is set when the integrated control detects an unexpected combination of R, W, G, and Y inputs from the thermostat — for example W energized without R, or W flickering on and off. The system suspends heat operation until a stable call is restored.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Loose or corroded thermostat wire at the furnace
Damaged thermostat cable in the wall

symptoms: Furnace ignores heat calls or short-cycles unexpectedly
Thermostat screen flickers or loses time
Heat sometimes runs, sometimes does nothing
Repeated lockouts that clear with a power cycle

fixSteps.title: Reseat Thermostat Wires
fixSteps.instruction: At both the furnace control and the thermostat, loosen each terminal, straighten the conductor, and re-tighten. Pay attention to R and W in particular.

fixSteps.title: Bypass Test the Thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, then briefly jumper R to W at the furnace. If the furnace fires normally, the thermostat or its cable is the culprit.

fixSteps.title: Replace Batteries / Add C-Wire
fixSteps.instruction: If the thermostat is battery-powered or smart, install fresh batteries or confirm a healthy C-wire. Many smart thermostats false-trigger when undervolted.

fixSteps.title: Measure 24 VAC
fixSteps.instruction: At R-C, expect 24–28 VAC. Below 20 VAC indicates a weak transformer or a shorted accessory drawing too much current.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Thermostat or Cable
fixSteps.instruction: If the bypass test confirmed it, replace the thermostat or pull a new 18/5 cable. Always cap unused conductors.

whenToCallPro: If 24 VAC is missing at the thermostat, if running new cable through finished walls is required, or if the fault persists after thermostat replacement.

faq.q: My new smart thermostat caused this — why?
faq.a: Many smart thermostats need a C-wire for steady power. Without one, they pulse-load R, which some boards interpret as faults.

faq.q: Can I diagnose without a multimeter?
faq.a: Partially. The R-to-W jumper test is the simplest field check, but voltage measurement is the most definitive.

faq.q: Why does it work after a reset, then fail again?
faq.a: Intermittent connections often pass during a quick reset and reopen as the components warm up.

title: Open Limit Switch — Overheat Detected
shortDescription: The high-limit switch opened because supply-air temperature exceeded the safe threshold.
fullDescription: This Trane fault posts when the high-limit switch detects supply-air temperature above the design ceiling, usually because airflow across the heat exchanger is too low. The control turns the gas off, runs the blower to purge heat, and reports the limit-trip code until temperatures normalize.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Severely clogged air filter restricting return airflow
Closed or blocked supply registers / collapsed flex duct
Failed or weak blower motor / capacitor

symptoms: Furnace fires briefly then shuts down
Blower runs long after the burners cut off
Hot air from supply registers followed by cold air
Burner cycle time noticeably shorter than normal

fixSteps.title: Replace the Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect and replace the return-air filter with the correct size and MERV rating. A 1" filter clogged with dust is the single most common cause.

fixSteps.title: Open All Supply Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the home and confirm every supply register is open and unblocked by furniture, rugs, or curtains. Closing too many registers raises static pressure dramatically.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the Blower Wheel
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, remove the blower assembly and check the wheel for caked dust. A coated wheel can lose 30%+ of its airflow.

fixSteps.title: Test Blower Motor and Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure capacitor microfarads and confirm they are within 6% of rated. Verify the motor reaches commanded RPM at heat speed.

fixSteps.title: Verify the Limit Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Check continuity across the limit switch at room temperature; it should be closed. If open cold, replace with the exact OEM part — limit switches are calibrated to the cabinet.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is verified normal but the limit still trips, the heat exchanger may be cracked or the gas input is overfired — both require a licensed technician.

faq.q: Can I jumper the limit switch to keep heat?
faq.a: No. Bypassing the limit can cause heat-exchanger damage and carbon-monoxide release.

faq.q: How often should I change my filter?
faq.a: Every 1–3 months for 1" pleated filters; 4–6 months for thicker media filters.

faq.q: Why does the blower keep running after lockout?
faq.a: It is intentionally purging residual heat from the heat exchanger to protect components.

title: Pressure Switch Did Not Close
shortDescription: The draft pressure switch did not close within the allowed window after the inducer started.
fullDescription: This Trane fault means the inducer motor energized but the pressure switch never sensed enough negative pressure to close its contacts. The control aborts the trial-for-ignition because operating without confirmed venting can release combustion gases into the home.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Blocked exhaust or intake terminal (snow, ice, debris, nest)
Plugged condensate trap on a high-efficiency model

symptoms: Inducer runs continuously without burner ignition
Furnace cycles inducer on and off chasing the switch
No heat output even though the thermostat is calling
Water dripping or pooling near a high-efficiency unit

fixSteps.title: Inspect Vent Terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Walk outside and verify the exhaust and intake pipes are clear of snow, leaves, and animal nests. Clear any obstruction with a non-metallic tool.

fixSteps.title: Check the Pressure Switch Hose
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the small rubber hose from the pressure switch, blow through it to clear water, and confirm it is firmly seated at both ends.

fixSteps.title: Service the Condensate Trap
fixSteps.instruction: On 90%+ efficiency furnaces, pour a cup of warm water through the inducer drain port to flush the trap. Reinstall and confirm free drainage.

fixSteps.title: Measure Switch Operation
fixSteps.instruction: With the inducer running, measure differential pressure at the switch port; compare to the spec on the switch (often -0.40 to -1.20 inches WC). Below spec means inducer or venting issue, not a bad switch.

fixSteps.title: Replace Inducer or Switch as Needed
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the pressure switch only if the differential pressure is correct but contacts will not close. Otherwise replace the inducer assembly with the OEM part.

whenToCallPro: If venting and condensate are clear but the switch still will not close, an inducer or board issue is likely and should be diagnosed by a licensed technician.

faq.q: Why does this happen more often in winter?
faq.a: Snow drifts and ice can block sidewall vent terminations, especially during heavy storms.

faq.q: Can I bypass the pressure switch with a jumper?
faq.a: Never. The switch is the primary safety preventing operation with blocked venting and CO buildup.

faq.q: My condensate line freezes outdoors — what now?
faq.a: Re-route the condensate to an interior drain. Frozen condensate is a common cause of repeated pressure-switch faults.

title: Flame Rollout Switch Tripped
shortDescription: A flame rollout switch detected flame outside the burner enclosure and shut the furnace down.
fullDescription: This Trane fault is one of the most serious furnace faults. A rollout switch — a one-time or manual-reset thermal device near the burner box — opened because flame escaped the heat exchanger. Causes include blocked heat exchanger, weak inducer, or cracked exchanger. Operation must not resume until the cause is identified by a technician.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off the gas supply before attempting any repairs.

causes.cause: Severely sooted or blocked heat exchanger passages
Failed or weak inducer motor (insufficient draft)

symptoms: Furnace will not restart even after power cycling
Soot or scorch marks on the burner cover
Burnt smell near the furnace
Yellow rather than blue flame at the burners

fixSteps.title: Stop Using the Furnace
fixSteps.instruction: Switch the system off at the thermostat and the disconnect. Close the gas supply at the unit shutoff. Do not attempt to reset the rollout switch.

fixSteps.title: Verify CO Detector Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Test all CO detectors on the level with the furnace. If any alarm or read above 9 ppm, ventilate the home and call for service immediately.

fixSteps.title: Document the Symptom
fixSteps.instruction: Note any soot, melted wiring, or warped sheet metal near the burners. Photos help the technician diagnose faster.

fixSteps.title: Schedule Professional Service
fixSteps.instruction: A flame rollout requires a combustion analysis, draft test, and heat-exchanger inspection — all licensed-tech work.

fixSteps.title: Do Not Bypass the Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Resetting or jumping the rollout switch without correcting the cause can lead to a fire and CO release. Wait for service.

repairTime: Professional service same-day to several days
whenToCallPro: Always. Flame rollout is never a DIY repair — there is no safe way to operate the furnace until a technician has inspected the heat exchanger and venting.

faq.q: Why is rollout so dangerous?
faq.a: Flame outside the burner box can ignite nearby materials and indicates that combustion gases — including CO — may be entering the home.

faq.q: Will the rollout switch reset itself?
faq.a: Most modern rollout switches are manual-reset only. The technician will reset after correcting the underlying issue.

faq.q: Could a dirty filter cause this?
faq.a: Indirectly. Restricted airflow over time can warp the heat exchanger, leading to cracks that allow rollout.

title: Flame Roll-Out Switch Tripped
shortDescription: A roll-out limit detected flames escaping the burner box and tripped the manual-reset safety switch.
fullDescription: The flame roll-out switch is a manual-reset thermal safety mounted at the front of the burner assembly. When flames or hot gases escape the combustion chamber instead of being drawn into the heat exchanger, the switch trips and de-energizes the gas valve. Common causes include a blocked heat exchanger, weak draft inducer, or cracked heat exchanger.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Weak or failing draft inducer motor
Restricted flue or vent terminal (snow, nest, debris)

symptoms: Furnace will not light and burner area shows soot
Hot smell or scorched paint near the burner box
Manual-reset button on the burner-area switch has popped out
Repeated lockouts on cold days only

fixSteps.title: Shut Off Power and Gas
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace power switch and close the gas shutoff before opening the burner compartment.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Burner Area
fixSteps.instruction: Look for soot, scorched insulation, or melted wires around the burners — these are signs of flame roll-out.

fixSteps.title: Check Vent Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the exhaust and intake terminals outdoors for blockage. Clear snow, nests, or debris.

fixSteps.title: Reset the Switch
fixSteps.instruction: After confirming no damage and clear vents, press the manual reset button on the roll-out switch firmly until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Have Heat Exchanger Inspected
fixSteps.instruction: If the switch trips again, stop using the furnace and have a licensed technician perform a heat-exchanger integrity inspection.

whenToCallPro: If the switch trips a second time, the heat exchanger is suspect — call a licensed technician immediately. A cracked exchanger is a carbon-monoxide hazard.

faq.q: Can I keep running the furnace with this code?
faq.a: If the furnace still produces heat, you can run it short-term, but address the issue promptly because related safety circuits may shut it down without warning.

faq.q: Will resetting the furnace clear this?
faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.

title: High-Limit Switch Open — Overheat Condition
shortDescription: The plenum high-limit switch opened due to excessive supply-air temperature.
fullDescription: The high-limit switch is a normally-closed thermal safety in the supply plenum. When supply-air temperature climbs above the rated limit (typically 160-200°F), the switch opens to shut off the gas valve and prevent damage to the heat exchanger. The blower continues running to dissipate heat. Repeated trips usually mean restricted airflow rather than a faulty switch.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Dirty or clogged air filter restricting return airflow
Closed or blocked supply registers / undersized return duct
Failed or slow blower motor (bad capacitor, bearings)
Incorrect blower speed tap for installed system

symptoms: Burners light then shut off after 1-3 minutes while blower keeps running
Supply registers feel very hot then very cool
Furnace short-cycles on heat call
Cabinet noticeably hotter than normal

fixSteps.title: Replace the Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the filter and check for restriction. Replace any filter older than 60 days or visibly grey.

fixSteps.title: Open All Supply Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the home and confirm every supply register is fully open and unobstructed by furniture or rugs.

fixSteps.title: Verify Return-Air Path
fixSteps.instruction: Check that return grilles are not blocked and that the blower-compartment door is fully sealed.

fixSteps.title: Measure Temperature Rise
fixSteps.instruction: With a thermometer, measure return and supply temperatures during a heat call. Compare against the data plate's listed rise (typically 30-60°F).

fixSteps.title: Test Blower and Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: If temperature rise is too high, test the run capacitor and inspect the blower wheel for buildup. Replace components as needed.

whenToCallPro: If airflow is unrestricted but the limit still trips, call a technician to verify gas input pressure and check for a failing blower or undersized ductwork.

title: ECM Blower Motor Communication Fault
shortDescription: The control board has lost communication with the variable-speed ECM blower motor.
fullDescription: Modern furnaces use ECM (Electronically Commutated Motor) blowers that communicate with the control board over a low-voltage signal harness. When the board cannot read motor RPM feedback or the motor's onboard module fails to acknowledge speed commands, the system flags an ECM communication fault and falls back to either off or a fixed safety speed.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Loose or corroded ECM motor harness connector
Failed ECM motor control module (back of motor)
Control board ECM driver section failed
Voltage spike from recent storm or power event

symptoms: Blower will not run on heat or cool calls
Blower runs at one fixed speed regardless of mode
Audible chirping or single-rotation pulse from motor
Diagnostic code on board indicates motor / ECM fault

fixSteps.title: Cycle Power for 60 Seconds
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace breaker for one full minute to allow the ECM module to fully discharge and reinitialize.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Motor Harness
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, unplug and reseat both the 5-pin power and 16-pin control connectors at the motor. Look for burned pins or moisture.

fixSteps.title: Check Capacitor (PSC fallback models)
fixSteps.instruction: On hybrid models with a run capacitor, test it for proper microfarad rating.

fixSteps.title: Test for 120/240V at Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm correct line voltage at the motor's power plug during a call for blower.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor or Module
fixSteps.instruction: If line voltage is present and signals are correct but the motor is silent, the ECM module or motor must be replaced.

whenToCallPro: If reseating connectors does not restore communication, ECM motors must be matched to the model and replaced by a qualified technician.

faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.

title: Condensate Overflow Switch Open
shortDescription: A float or overflow switch detected high water in the condensate pan or drain trap.
fullDescription: High-efficiency (90%+) furnaces produce condensate that must drain freely. A float switch in the secondary drain pan or inline trap will open and shut down the furnace if water backs up. Common causes are a clogged condensate trap, blocked drain line, frozen drain in winter, or a failed condensate pump.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Clogged condensate trap with biological slime
Blocked or kinked drain hose to floor drain or pump
Failed condensate pump (motor or check valve)

symptoms: Furnace will not start; water visible in secondary pan or under unit
Gurgling sounds during inducer startup
Pressure-switch or limit faults that clear after pumping out water
Condensate pump hums but does not move water

fixSteps.title: Pump Out Standing Water
fixSteps.instruction: Use a wet/dry vac to remove water from the secondary pan and the drain trap inlet.

fixSteps.title: Clean the Condensate Trap
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the trap, flush with warm water and a small amount of distilled vinegar, then reinstall.

fixSteps.title: Clear Drain Line
fixSteps.instruction: Run a thin brush or shop vac through the entire drain line to the termination point.

fixSteps.title: Test Condensate Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Pour water directly into the pump reservoir; the pump should activate and discharge water within seconds.

fixSteps.title: Verify Float Switch
fixSteps.instruction: With trap clear, jumper the float switch terminals briefly to confirm operation, then restore wiring.

whenToCallPro: If the drain repeatedly clogs, a technician can re-pitch the trap, add a cleanout, or upsize the line. Frozen exterior runs may require heat tape or a redesign.

faq.a: If the furnace still produces heat, you can run it short-term, but address the issue promptly because related safety circuits may shut it down without warning.

faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.

title: Line-Voltage Polarity Reversed or Open Ground
shortDescription: Control board detected reversed hot/neutral or a missing equipment ground.
fullDescription: The control board uses the chassis ground as a reference for flame-rectification sensing. If line voltage is wired with hot and neutral reversed, or if the equipment ground is open, the flame signal cannot be read reliably and the board flags a polarity / ground fault before allowing ignition.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Hot and neutral reversed at outlet, disconnect, or whip
Loose neutral at panel or junction box
Use of an ungrounded extension cord (temporary install)
Failed surge protector creating impedance on neutral

symptoms: Furnace will not progress past initial diagnostic
Code clears momentarily then returns when neighbor's appliance starts
Faint shock when touching cabinet (open ground)
Flame proves intermittently and drops out

fixSteps.title: Verify Power at Service Switch
fixSteps.instruction: With a multimeter on the line side of the furnace switch, confirm 120V hot-to-neutral, 120V hot-to-ground, and 0V neutral-to-ground.

fixSteps.title: Test Receptacle Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: If the furnace is cord-connected, plug a 3-light receptacle tester into the outlet to verify wiring.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Ground Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Open the furnace junction box and confirm the bare or green ground wire is firmly attached to the chassis ground screw.

fixSteps.title: Correct Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: If polarity is reversed at the outlet or disconnect, shut off the breaker and swap the hot and neutral conductors at the device.

fixSteps.title: Power Up and Retest
fixSteps.instruction: Restore power and verify the code clears and ignition completes normally.

whenToCallPro: If your service feed itself shows reversed polarity or a floating neutral, contact your utility or a licensed electrician — do not work inside the panel.

title: Communicating Bus Fault Between Thermostat and Furnace
shortDescription: The communicating thermostat cannot reliably exchange data with the furnace control.
fullDescription: Communicating systems use a 2-wire data bus (often labeled 1/2 or A/B) to exchange staging, fan, and diagnostic data between the thermostat, indoor unit, and outdoor unit. Wiring errors, polarity reversal on the data pair, or interference from a thermostat 'C-wire' adapter can break communication and force the system to a non-communicating fallback or full lockout.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Data wires reversed at thermostat or furnace terminal
Long wire run with too small a gauge causing voltage drop
Thermostat firmware mismatched with control board
Failed thermostat or control board communication chip
Damaged thermostat cable (staple through, rodent damage)

symptoms: Thermostat displays 'communication error', 'No comm', or blank screen
Furnace runs only on emergency / non-communicating mode
Outdoor unit will not stage up despite cold temperatures
Intermittent operation that improves after a power cycle

fixSteps.title: Power-Cycle Both Ends
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the furnace breaker AND remove the thermostat from its base for 60 seconds, then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Verify Wire Landings
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the data pair lands on the matching terminals at both the thermostat and the furnace control.

fixSteps.title: Check for Damaged Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the thermostat cable along its run for staples, kinks, or chew marks. Replace any damaged section.

fixSteps.title: Update or Match Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If the brand offers a firmware update via the thermostat menu or app, run it. Otherwise verify model compatibility.

fixSteps.title: Substitute Thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: If a known-good thermostat communicates correctly, the original thermostat is at fault.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is correct and both thermostat and board are confirmed compatible, the comm chip on the control board may be failed and require replacement.

title: Draft Inducer Locked Rotor or Out-of-Range Current
shortDescription: The control measured inducer current outside the expected range, indicating a stalled or shorted motor.
fullDescription: The control board monitors current draw on the draft inducer. When current is too low (open winding, broken connection) or too high (locked rotor, shorted winding, debris jamming the wheel), the board aborts the heat call and flags an inducer-fault code. Continuing to run a stalled motor can melt the housing or trip the breaker.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Inducer wheel obstructed by debris (insulation, leaves)
Loose motor wiring at control board

symptoms: Inducer hums but does not spin, or spins very slowly
Breaker trips when furnace calls for heat
Smell of hot motor windings near the inducer
Pressure switch never closes because draft is too weak

fixSteps.title: Cut Power Immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off the furnace switch to prevent further damage to the stalled motor.

fixSteps.title: Check for Obstruction
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, remove the inducer cover and verify the wheel spins freely by hand.

fixSteps.title: Test the Run Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: If the inducer uses a capacitor, measure microfarads. Replace if more than 10% out of spec.

fixSteps.title: Measure Motor Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: With leads disconnected, ohm out the motor windings; an open or near-zero reading means the motor is bad.

fixSteps.title: Replace Inducer Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: If the motor is seized or burned, replace the entire inducer assembly with the OEM part for that model.

whenToCallPro: A burned-smelling motor or repeatedly tripping breaker requires professional replacement to avoid fire risk.

title: Twinning Wire / Phase Mismatch Between Paired Units
shortDescription: Two furnaces wired to share a single thermostat are out of phase or twinning wire is open.
fullDescription: Some homes use two furnaces ducted into a common plenum and 'twinned' so they fire together. The twinning wire synchronizes the two control boards so blowers and ignition run simultaneously. If line-voltage phasing is mismatched between the two units or the twinning conductor opens, one or both units will lock out with a twinning fault.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Twinning wire broken, disconnected, or wrong terminal
Two units fed from opposite legs of 240V split-phase service
Different control board firmware between paired units
Only one of two breakers tripped or off

symptoms: One furnace runs and the other does not, despite both calling
Both units fault simultaneously on heat call
Diagnostic LED indicates twinning or phase fault
Erratic blower behavior — one blower starts, the other coasts

fixSteps.title: Verify Both Breakers On
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm both furnace breakers are fully on and the service switches are closed.

fixSteps.title: Check Twinning Wire
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect the dedicated twinning conductor between the two control boards for proper landing and continuity.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Phase Match
fixSteps.instruction: At each furnace, measure hot-to-ground; both should read the same nominal voltage from the same leg of the panel.

fixSteps.title: Equalize Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If the boards are different revisions, contact the manufacturer for matched-firmware replacements.

fixSteps.title: Test Twinned Operation
fixSteps.instruction: After repairs, force a heat call and confirm both units ignite, run, and shut down together.

whenToCallPro: Correcting service-leg phasing requires opening the panel and should be done by a licensed electrician.

title: Two-Stage Gas Valve Failure to Switch Stages
shortDescription: The control board commanded high-fire but the gas valve stayed on low-fire, or vice versa.
fullDescription: Two-stage and modulating gas valves use one or more low-voltage solenoids to switch between firing rates. The control board monitors flame current and stage-feedback to confirm the valve responded. If the valve fails to switch within the timing window, the system either runs single-stage as a fallback or locks out depending on how many calls fail.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Failed second-stage solenoid coil in the valve
Loose or corroded HI/LO wires at the gas valve
Control board not outputting 24V on stage-2 terminal
Gas pressure too low to support high-fire

symptoms: Furnace appears to run continuously without reaching setpoint
Flame size visibly does not change between stages
Long heat cycles in cold weather despite proper sizing
Stage-1 only operation indicated on diagnostic readout

fixSteps.title: Reset Control Board
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle the furnace and observe the next heat call to see whether stage-2 attempts to engage.

fixSteps.title: Verify Stage Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the HI and LO conductors are landed on the correct terminals at both the valve and the board.

fixSteps.title: Measure 24V at Stage-2
fixSteps.instruction: During a stage-2 call, measure 24V across the HI solenoid terminals; absence of voltage means the board is at fault.

fixSteps.title: Test Manifold Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: A technician should manometer the manifold on both stages and compare to the rating plate.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Gas Valve
fixSteps.instruction: If 24V is present but the stage does not change and pressure is correct upstream, replace the gas valve.

whenToCallPro: Any gas valve replacement or manometer test must be done by a licensed gas technician — leak testing is mandatory after reassembly.

title: Outdoor / Supply Thermistor Out of Range
shortDescription: A temperature sensor used by the furnace is reading outside its valid range, blocking proper staging.
fullDescription: Modern furnaces use NTC thermistors on the supply plenum and (on heat-pump systems) on the outdoor coil to optimize staging, blower speed, and dual-fuel switchover. When a thermistor reads as a short (~0Ω) or open (∞Ω), the board cannot calculate temperature and either reverts to default behavior or shuts down depending on which sensor failed.
safetyWarning: Gas furnace safety: If you smell gas, leave the home immediately and call your gas company from outside. Do not operate any electrical switches. Always turn off power and gas at the appliance shutoffs before servicing internal components.

causes.cause: Sensor wire pinched in cabinet or chewed by rodents
Sensor dislodged from clip or well
Wrong sensor type installed (different resistance curve)

symptoms: Furnace runs but blower stays on lowest speed regardless of demand
Dual-fuel system never crosses over to gas heat below balance point
Diagnostic readout shows -40°F or 200°F when ambient is moderate
Sensor-fault icon on the thermostat or control display

fixSteps.title: Locate the Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Refer to the wiring diagram on the blower door to find the affected thermistor.

fixSteps.title: Inspect and Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the sensor, examine the pins for green corrosion, and reseat firmly into the connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Resistance at Room Temp
fixSteps.instruction: With sensor disconnected from the board, measure resistance and compare against the model's resistance-vs-temperature chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace the Thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install an OEM replacement of the matching type and reconnect the harness.

fixSteps.title: Verify Reading on Diagnostic Display
fixSteps.instruction: Power up and confirm the reported temperature on the board's readout matches the actual ambient.

whenToCallPro: If multiple sensors read out of range simultaneously, the control board's analog input is suspect and should be tested by a technician.
