faq.a: A power-cycle reset may clear a temporary fault, but if the underlying condition (sensor, motor, valve, vent) is still present the code will return on the next call for heat.

title: Low-Stage Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: Low-stage pressure switch failed to close when low-stage inducer started.
fullDescription: On a two-stage Trane furnace, the control board energizes the low-stage inducer and expects the low-stage pressure switch to close within a set time window. When the switch remains open, the board halts ignition. Common causes are a blocked condensate trap, restricted venting, a cracked pressure switch hose, or a weak inducer motor that cannot pull adequate negative pressure on low fire.
safetyWarning: Combustion safety: do not bypass or jumper a pressure switch. A stuck-open switch may indicate a blocked flue, which can spill carbon monoxide into the home. If you suspect CO, evacuate and ventilate the space.

causes.cause: Blocked or kinked pressure switch hose
Condensate drain trap clogged with biofilm
Inducer motor wheel dirty or wearing out
Restricted intake or exhaust vent termination

symptoms: Inducer motor runs but ignition never starts
Furnace cycles off after about 60 seconds
Diagnostic LED reports low-stage pressure fault
Heat call ends with no flame established
Visible water in burner box or near collector box

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pressure Switch Hose
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the hose from the pressure switch and check it for kinks, cracks, or condensate. Blow it clear and reseat tightly.

fixSteps.title: Clear Condensate Trap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the condensate trap, flush with warm water and a mild vinegar solution, and reinstall. Verify the drain line slopes downward to the floor drain.

fixSteps.title: Test Inducer Draft
fixSteps.instruction: With a manometer, measure inducer pressure at the switch port during a heat call. Compare to the value printed on the switch body.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Vent Terminations
fixSteps.instruction: Walk to the intake and exhaust outside the home and clear snow, leaves, insects, or animal nests. Confirm proper clearances per the install manual.

fixSteps.title: Replace Pressure Switch
fixSteps.instruction: If draft is correct but the switch will not close at the rated value, replace the switch with the exact OEM part number listed in the wiring diagram.

whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if draft pressure tests below spec, if the inducer motor is noisy, or if you suspect a partial flue blockage.

faq.q: Is a stuck-open low-stage pressure switch dangerous?
faq.a: It is a safety feature working correctly. The danger is when someone bypasses it; that defeats blocked-flue protection and can allow carbon monoxide spillage.

faq.q: Can I clean instead of replace the switch?
faq.a: The switch is a sealed diaphragm and is not field-serviceable. You can clean the hose and port, but the switch itself must be replaced if defective.

faq.q: Why only on low stage?
faq.a: Low fire produces less inducer suction, so a marginal blockage or weak inducer first shows up on the low-stage circuit before high stage fails.

title: Secondary Limit Switch Open
shortDescription: Auxiliary high-limit switch in the blower or supply plenum has tripped.
fullDescription: The Trane furnace control board is reading the secondary (auxiliary) limit switch as open. This switch is mounted in the blower compartment or supply plenum and protects against overheating when airflow is restricted or the blower is failing. Common triggers are a clogged filter, closed registers, slipping blower wheel, or a failing blower capacitor on PSC models.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass a tripped limit. Repeated overheating can crack the heat exchanger, which is a carbon monoxide hazard.

causes.cause: Blower wheel dirty or loose on shaft
Limit switch itself out of calibration

symptoms: Furnace shuts off mid heat cycle on overheat
Burner lights then extinguishes within minutes
Cabinet feels unusually hot to the touch
Blower runs but airflow at registers is weak
Repeated short cycling without lockout

fixSteps.title: Replace Air Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Slide out the existing filter and install a fresh one of the size and MERV rating recommended by Trane. Note the install date.

fixSteps.title: Open All Supply Registers
fixSteps.instruction: Walk through the home and open every supply register at least 80%. Closing more than 20% of registers can starve airflow.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Blower Wheel
fixSteps.instruction: Cut power, remove the blower assembly, and inspect the squirrel-cage wheel. Clean caked dust with a soft brush; check setscrew on the motor shaft.

fixSteps.title: Test Blower Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: On PSC blowers, discharge and measure the run capacitor with a meter that has a capacitance setting. Replace if outside ±6% of rated microfarads.

fixSteps.title: Verify Limit Switch
fixSteps.instruction: Measure continuity across the limit switch when the furnace is cold. It should read closed; if open at room temperature, replace with the exact OEM part.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the blower motor is failing, if the heat exchanger appears discolored or rust-streaked, or if the limit trips again after cleaning.

faq.q: How often should I replace the filter?
faq.a: 1-inch pleated filters typically need replacement every 60–90 days. Thicker media filters last 6–12 months.

faq.q: Why does the blower keep running after shutdown?
faq.a: When the limit trips, the blower runs continuously to cool the heat exchanger. That is normal protective behavior.

faq.q: Can a closed register really overheat the furnace?
faq.a: Yes. Closing too many registers raises static pressure, reduces airflow over the heat exchanger, and trips the limit.

title: Flame Rollout Switch Tripped
shortDescription: A rollout sensor near the burners has detected flames outside the heat exchanger.
fullDescription: The flame rollout switches mounted above the burners on the Trane furnace have opened, indicating that combustion gases or flames have escaped the heat exchanger. This is a hard-lockout safety condition that requires manual reset and immediate diagnosis. Common causes include a blocked flue, a failed inducer, a cracked heat exchanger, or severe burner soot buildup.
safetyWarning: Critical safety condition. Do not reset and run the furnace repeatedly. A rollout almost always indicates blocked combustion airflow or a damaged heat exchanger and may produce carbon monoxide.

causes.cause: Heavily blocked flue or vent pipe
Inducer motor not running or running too slow
Burner ports clogged with rust or spider webs

symptoms: Furnace lights briefly then locks out immediately
Soot or scorch marks visible above burner box
Smell of unburnt gas or hot metal near furnace
Manual reset button popped out on rollout switch
CO detector activates near the appliance

fixSteps.title: Shut Off Gas Supply
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the gas shutoff valve perpendicular to the gas line. Do not relight until the cause is found and corrected.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Flue System
fixSteps.instruction: From outside the home, check for snow, ice dams, or animal nests in the vent termination. Inside, look for soot at joints.

fixSteps.title: Check Inducer Operation
fixSteps.instruction: Power the unit, call for heat, and confirm the inducer spins freely and quietly. If it hums or stalls, replace it.

fixSteps.title: Visually Inspect Heat Exchanger
fixSteps.instruction: Using a borescope or flashlight, inspect each cell of the heat exchanger for cracks, rust-out, or scaling.

fixSteps.title: Reset Only After Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Press the rollout button only after the underlying cause is corrected. If it trips again, shut the unit down and call a professional.

whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician immediately. Heat-exchanger inspection and combustion analysis require professional tools and certification.

faq.q: Can I just press the reset button?
faq.a: Only after the cause is identified and fixed. Repeatedly resetting a rollout switch without correcting the issue is unsafe.

faq.q: Will my warranty cover heat exchanger replacement?
faq.a: Most Trane furnaces carry a limited 20-year or lifetime heat-exchanger warranty for the original homeowner. Labor is typically not covered.

faq.q: How does a rollout actually happen?
faq.a: If exhaust gases cannot leave through the flue, they back up and burn out the front of the burner box, tripping the sensor.

title: Line Voltage Polarity Reversed
shortDescription: Hot and neutral conductors are swapped at the furnace power connection.
fullDescription: The Trane control board uses neutral as a reference for flame sensing. When line and neutral are swapped at the disconnect or service panel, the flame signal microamp reading collapses and the board reports a polarity or grounding fault. The unit will not run until polarity is corrected.
safetyWarning: Electrical hazard. Always shut off power at the breaker before checking polarity, and use a non-contact voltage tester to verify the circuit is dead.

causes.cause: Hot and neutral reversed at furnace disconnect
Reversed polarity at the service panel breaker
Missing or open ground at the furnace
Wiring error after a recent service or remodel

symptoms: Control board displays polarity or grounding fault
Furnace will not start any heat sequence
Flame signal microamps read zero or unstable
Issue began immediately after electrical work
Other gas appliances on same circuit also act up

fixSteps.title: Verify with a Plug-In Tester
fixSteps.instruction: Plug a three-prong outlet tester into a nearby receptacle on the same circuit and confirm correct wiring lights pattern.

fixSteps.title: Check Furnace Disconnect
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service switch and measure between hot, neutral, and ground with a multimeter once power is restored briefly.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wire Nuts at Junction Box
fixSteps.instruction: Open the wire-nut splices inside the burner-compartment junction box and confirm black-to-black, white-to-white, green-to-green.

fixSteps.title: Tighten or Replace Connections
fixSteps.instruction: Replace any wire nuts that show heat damage. Re-tighten lugs at the disconnect and breaker if accessible.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Ground Continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance between the chassis and the panel ground bar. Anything above a few ohms indicates an ineffective ground path.

whenToCallPro: Call a licensed electrician if the issue is at the service panel, if the ground is missing, or if you are not comfortable working in a live disconnect.

faq.q: Why does polarity matter on a 120V circuit?
faq.a: The flame-sense circuit references neutral. With swapped polarity, the rectified DC flame current cannot flow correctly, and the board sees no flame.

faq.q: Will a surge protector cause this?
faq.a: No, a surge device cannot reverse polarity. This is always a wiring issue.

faq.q: Can I run the furnace temporarily on reversed polarity?
faq.a: No. The board will lock out and even if it ran, you would have no flame-failure protection.

title: ECM Blower Communication Lost
shortDescription: Variable-speed ECM motor has lost serial communication with the control board.
fullDescription: The Trane control board cannot communicate with the variable-speed ECM blower module. Without serial data the motor either stops or runs at a default constant CFM. Causes include damaged or unseated 16-pin harness, water damage to the ECM control module, a failed motor end-bell, or a control-board low-voltage fault feeding the harness.
safetyWarning: ECM modules store charge for several minutes after power down. Wait at least five minutes after disconnecting power before handling.

causes.cause: Water dripped onto motor end-bell from condensate leak
Failed ECM control module (separate from rotor)
Damaged thermostat or zoning wiring at board
Control board ECM driver circuit failed

symptoms: Blower will not start or runs at fixed wrong speed
Diagnostic LED indicates blower communication fault
Motor hums for two seconds then stops
Burners light then shut down on temperature limit
Status LED on motor end-bell flashing fault pattern

fixSteps.title: Power Down Five Minutes
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the disconnect. Wait at least five minutes for the ECM bus capacitors to bleed before opening the motor.

fixSteps.title: Reseat the 16-Pin Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the harness at both the motor and the control board, inspect each pin for green corrosion, and seat firmly until the locking tab clicks.

fixSteps.title: Check for Condensate Drips
fixSteps.instruction: Look directly above the motor for evaporator coil drip pan rust or split refrigerant line insulation that could drip on the end-bell.

fixSteps.title: Test Module Independently
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the suspect ECM control module onto a known-good motor (or vice versa) following Trane's service guide.

fixSteps.title: Replace Module or Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Order the OEM ECM module or full motor matched to the model number on the data tag. Avoid generic replacements.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for any ECM module replacement; matching the part number to the appliance is critical and damaged modules can be expensive to misdiagnose.

faq.q: Is the ECM module the same as the motor?
faq.a: On most Trane units, the ECM is built as two halves: the rotor/stator end and the control module on the rear. Either can be replaced separately.

faq.q: Can I use a generic ECM motor?
faq.a: No. The control module is programmed with airflow tables specific to the furnace cabinet. A wrong module will move incorrect CFM.

faq.q: Why does water damage the ECM so often?
faq.a: The control module's electronics are not sealed against drips. A few drops on the connector can corrode pins overnight.

title: Gas Valve Relay Driver Fault
shortDescription: Control board has detected an open or shorted gas-valve relay output.
fullDescription: The Trane control board self-tests its gas-valve relay every cycle. When the contacts weld closed, fail open, or the coil reads outside expected resistance, the board enters a hard lockout to prevent unsafe valve operation. The board itself, the wiring harness, or the gas valve coil can each cause this fault.
safetyWarning: If the gas-valve relay is welded closed, the gas valve could be receiving power even when the board commands it off. Shut off the manual gas cock immediately if you smell gas.

causes.cause: Welded contacts inside the gas-valve relay
Loose harness on gas valve terminals
Excess current draw from a faulty valve

symptoms: Furnace locks out before the inducer even starts
Gas-valve fault LED stays on continuously
Repeated lockout immediately after manual reset
No 24V at gas valve during heat call
Audible chatter from gas valve coil

fixSteps.title: Cut Gas at Manual Cock
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the gas shutoff handle perpendicular to the line before troubleshooting any valve circuit.

fixSteps.title: Verify 24V at Valve
fixSteps.instruction: With a meter, check 24VAC across the valve terminals during a heat call. Compare to the schematic on the inside cover.

fixSteps.title: Measure Valve Coil Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the valve harness and measure resistance across the coil. Compare with the spec on Trane's service manual; values typically fall between 30 and 80 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wire Harness
fixSteps.instruction: Pull each terminal off and look for melted insulation, green corrosion, or pinched wires near sharp metal edges.

fixSteps.title: Replace Faulty Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the gas valve, the harness, or the control board based on the readings, using only OEM parts.

whenToCallPro: Call a licensed gas technician for any gas-valve work. Sealing pipe joints and pressure-testing the line are required after replacement.

faq.q: Can I replace just the relay on the board?
faq.a: Some boards use socketed relays, but most Trane models have soldered relays. Board replacement is usually the supported repair path.

faq.q: How do I know it is the valve and not the board?
faq.a: Measure coil resistance and 24V at the valve. If voltage is present and coil is in spec but valve does not open, the valve is at fault.

faq.q: Is it safe to bypass the lockout?
faq.a: No. The lockout exists to prevent unsafe gas operation. Diagnose and repair, do not jumper the safety circuit.

title: Twinned Furnace Out of Sync
shortDescription: Two Trane furnaces twinned on a single duct system are not communicating in step.
fullDescription: When two Trane furnaces share a return and supply duct (twinned), the control boards exchange data over a twin terminal. If the boards see mismatched cycles, mismatched dipswitch settings, or a broken twin wire, the system locks both units out to prevent one furnace from pulling combustion air backward through the other.
safetyWarning: Backdrafting through an idle furnace can pull carbon monoxide into the home. Do not run a twinned pair with the twin wire disconnected.

causes.cause: Open or miswired twin terminal between boards
Different dipswitch settings on the two boards
One thermostat wired to only one of the two units
Static pressure imbalance at the takeoffs

symptoms: Both furnaces lock out at start of heat call
One furnace runs while the other does not
Twinning fault code on both diagnostic LEDs
Loud whistle in the return duct on startup
Burners flicker and cycle off within seconds

fixSteps.title: Verify Twin Terminal Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm a single conductor between the TWIN terminals on each board, with no break and no extra connections.

fixSteps.title: Match Dipswitch Settings
fixSteps.instruction: Compare every dipswitch on both boards. They must be identical for blower CFM, heat rise, and stage rules.

fixSteps.title: Verify Both Boards Same Revision
fixSteps.instruction: Check the part number sticker on each control board. Different revisions can twin but firmware mismatch will fault.

fixSteps.title: Confirm Common Thermostat Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: The thermostat R, W, G, Y leads must land on the designated master furnace; the slave receives only the twin signal.

fixSteps.title: Balance Static Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: Measure return static at each cabinet. If one is starving, install a balancing damper or larger return drop.

whenToCallPro: Twinned systems should be set up by a licensed installer. Improper twinning can damage heat exchangers and create CO hazards.

faq.q: Why twin two furnaces?
faq.a: Some homes need more capacity than one cabinet provides, or a contractor uses two smaller units to fit a tight mechanical room.

faq.q: Can I run them as separate units?
faq.a: Only if the duct system is split. If they share return or supply, they must be twinned.

faq.q: Does twinning require thermostat upgrades?
faq.a: A standard 24V thermostat is fine; only the master receives stat wiring. The twin signal is internal between the boards.

title: Outdoor Air Thermistor Open
shortDescription: Optional outdoor temperature sensor reads outside its valid range.
fullDescription: The Trane control board's outdoor air thermistor, used for cold-weather lockout of heat-pump backup or for staged-heat economy, is reading open or shorted. The board defaults to a safe heating mode but logs the fault. Causes include broken wires from rodents at the attic chase, water in the splice cap, or an end-of-life thermistor element.
safetyWarning: Low-voltage circuit, but always ladder-safe practices apply when accessing the outdoor sensor at the eave or condenser.

causes.cause: Broken thermistor wire from rodent damage
Water-filled splice cap at outdoor unit
Loose terminal at control board OAT input

symptoms: Outdoor temp reads -40 or off scale on thermostat
Backup heat staging behaves erratically
Diagnostic LED flags OAT sensor fault
Heat pump runs in extreme cold without backup
Communicating thermostat shows sensor missing

fixSteps.title: Locate Sensor and Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor is typically taped to the outdoor unit or zip-tied near the condenser fan grille. Inspect for chewed insulation.

fixSteps.title: Open Splice and Dry Out
fixSteps.instruction: Cut off any water-filled splice cap, dry the conductors, and re-splice with a waterproof gel-filled connector.

fixSteps.title: Measure Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect at the board and measure across the leads. At 25 °C the value should match the spec table in the install manual (often 10 kΩ).

fixSteps.title: Replace Thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: If reading is open or wildly off, install a new OEM thermistor. Match length and resistance curve.

fixSteps.title: Configure Board
fixSteps.instruction: After replacement, set the OAT lockout setpoints in the installer menu per the homeowner's heat-pump control strategy.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor is in a hard-to-reach attic chase or if your system uses a communicating bus that needs configuration after replacement.

faq.q: Will the furnace run without the sensor?
faq.a: Yes, but heat-pump efficiency suffers because backup-heat lockout cannot be enforced.

faq.q: Can I substitute a generic 10K thermistor?
faq.a: Only if it has the same beta (B value) curve as the OEM. Otherwise temperature readings will be wrong.

faq.q: Why is the sensor outside?
faq.a: It measures actual outdoor air, not equipment-cabinet temperature, so the system can decide when to lock out the compressor.

title: Flame Loss During Run Cycle
shortDescription: Flame was established but extinguished mid-cycle, triggering a soft lockout.
fullDescription: The Trane control proved a flame at startup but later lost the flame signal during the run period. After three retries it enters a one-hour soft lockout. Causes range from a marginal flame sensor to gas-pressure droop when other large appliances cycle on, to an overly close-coupled vent producing unstable combustion.
safetyWarning: Avoid running the unit unattended while diagnosing. Repeated reignition wastes gas and can saturate the heat exchanger area with raw fuel.

causes.cause: Manifold gas pressure drift under load

symptoms: Furnace runs 1–3 minutes then shuts off
Soft-lockout fault clears after about an hour
Flame sensor microamps drop below 1.0 µA after warmup
Issue worsens on cold, windy days
Other gas appliances also flicker when furnace cycles

fixSteps.title: Polish the Flame Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the sensor, polish with a Scotch-Brite pad (not sandpaper), and reinstall. Do not bend the rod.

fixSteps.title: Measure Flame Current
fixSteps.instruction: Insert a meter in series with the flame-sense lead and read microamps with the burners running. Compare with the service-manual minimum.

fixSteps.title: Check Manifold Pressure
fixSteps.instruction: While the furnace fires, measure manifold pressure with a manometer. It must hold steady at the rating-plate value.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Vent Termination
fixSteps.instruction: Outside, verify that no temporary objects (snow piles, lawn equipment) cause downdraft. Recheck during high-wind events.

fixSteps.title: Verify Neutral Bond
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the neutral-to-ground bond at the main panel; a missing bond hurts flame rectification.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for manifold-pressure adjustments, vent rework, or any electrical bonding work at the service panel.

faq.q: How clean should a flame sensor be?
faq.a: Polished bright metal at the tip. Even a thin amber film on the sensor rod can drop microamps below the threshold.

faq.q: Is sandpaper okay for cleaning?
faq.a: Avoid sandpaper; it can leave abrasive residue and scratches that hold contaminants. A nylon abrasive pad is better.

faq.q: Why does the lockout last an hour?
faq.a: The control assumes intermittent gas-supply or sensor problems. The cooldown lets temperatures stabilize before retry.

title: Communicating Thermostat Bus Fault
shortDescription: Trane serial communication between thermostat and furnace has dropped.
fullDescription: On Trane communicating systems, the thermostat, furnace, and outdoor unit exchange data over a serial bus carried on the standard four-wire stat cable. A short, swap, polarity reversal, or noisy connection causes the bus to drop. The thermostat usually displays a generic communication fault while the furnace logs a related code.
safetyWarning: Communicating systems are still 24V class 2, but follow standard low-voltage practices and never twist live conductors together.

causes.cause: Loose terminal screw on furnace control board
Damaged thermostat cable from staples or rodents
Shared cable with another low-voltage device

symptoms: Thermostat shows 'No communication' or blank screen
Furnace control LED flashes a comm-loss code
Heat or cool calls do not initiate
Communicating outdoor unit also faults out
Issue began after thermostat replacement

fixSteps.title: Verify Wire Order
fixSteps.instruction: Open the thermostat and confirm conductors land on the labeled terminals matching the furnace board exactly.

fixSteps.title: Tighten Furnace Board Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, then tighten each low-voltage screw on the control board's stat block.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Cable Run
fixSteps.instruction: Walk the visible portions of the thermostat cable, looking for staples that pierced insulation or kinks under carpet.

fixSteps.title: Run a Temporary Wire
fixSteps.instruction: If the home run is suspect, drop a temporary length of new four-conductor cable to isolate the wiring as the cause.

fixSteps.title: Measure Transformer Output
fixSteps.instruction: With the thermostat unplugged, measure 24VAC at the R-C terminals. Replace the transformer if reading is below 22V.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the cable run is concealed in finished walls or if the system also uses a communicating outdoor unit and zoning panel.

faq.q: Can I use any thermostat with a communicating furnace?
faq.a: Only the matched Trane communicating stat (or equivalent partner brand) supports full features. A generic stat works only if you switch the board to non-communicating mode.

faq.q: Does the bus need its own cable?
faq.a: Standard 18/4 thermostat wire is fine, but it must not be shared with humidifiers or other accessories that introduce noise.

faq.q: Is polarity important on the bus?
faq.a: Yes. Some Trane systems use a polarized bus. Reversing the data leads will drop communications.
